definitions.explanation: An attack using artillery, cannons, or large-caliber weapons. Refers to sustained fire from heavy weapons directed at a target or area.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}の{砲撃|ほうげき}が{始|はじ}まった。
{市街地|しがいち}への{砲撃|ほうげき}で{多|おお}くの{犠牲者|ぎせいしゃ}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: The shelling of urban areas caused many casualties.

examples.japanese: {停戦|ていせん}{合意|ごうい}にもかかわらず、{断続的|だんぞくてき}な{砲撃|ほうげき}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Despite the ceasefire agreement, intermittent shelling continues.

notes:
Composed of {砲|ほう} (cannon, artillery) and {撃|げき} (attack, strike). A military term frequently encountered in news coverage of armed conflicts and in historical accounts of battles.

USAGE:
Commonly appears in news reports about wars and conflicts. Also used as a する verb: {砲撃|ほうげき}する (to shell, to bombard).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {砲撃|ほうげき}を{受|う}ける — to come under shelling
- {砲撃|ほうげき}を{加|くわ}える — to carry out shelling
- {激|はげ}しい{砲撃|ほうげき} — fierce bombardment
- {砲撃|ほうげき}{音|おん} — sound of shelling

RELATED TERMS:
- {爆撃|ばくげき} — bombing (from aircraft)
- {空襲|くうしゅう} — air raid
- {攻撃|こうげき} — attack; the general term for any military attack
- {銃撃|じゅうげき} — shooting, gunfire (small arms)
